extraction.name: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark)
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating text embedding models across 8 embedding tasks (bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization) covering 58 datasets and 112 languages.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark aggregates 58 existing datasets across multiple tasks (classification, retrieval, clustering, pair classification, reranking, and summarization). Data sources include Reddit posts, Amazon reviews, Twitter posts, arXiv papers, bioRxiv/medRxiv papers, Stack Exchange posts, and other publicly available datasets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes text from multiple sources: Reddit posts (title+post concatenations), Amazon product reviews and counterfactual statements, Twitter posts, academic papers from arXiv/bioRxiv/medRxiv, Stack Exchange questions, IMDB movie reviews, banking queries, emotion statements, and various other text corpora across different domains and languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 2003-2018 for at least one component dataset (MedrxivClusteringP2P)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Dataset similarities and potential biases exist across MTEB datasets. Several datasets rely on the same corpora (e.g., ClimateFEVER and FEVER), resulting in high similarity scores. Clusters of similar datasets appear among CQADupstack variations and STS datasets. Scientific datasets show high similarities among each other even when coming from different tasks. The scale of experiments and model pre-training makes controlling for data contamination challenging, with overlap between MTEB datasets and model training datasets not controlled for in MTEB scores.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MTEB has several limitations: (1) Data contamination between training and evaluation datasets is not fully controlled due to the scale of experiments; (2) Some models may have seen parts of MTEB datasets during training (e.g., MPNet and MiniLM on SciDocsRR); (3) The benchmark assumes these contamination effects are insignificant when averaged across enough datasets; (4) Models are evaluated on test splits except MSMARCO which uses dev split; (5) The benchmark imposes no limit on input length, leaving truncation decisions to individual models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: MTEB includes multilingual datasets covering 112 languages, which inherently involves language as a sensitive attribute. Some classification datasets include sentiment analysis and toxic conversation detection tasks that may involve sensitive content.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is designed for evaluating text embedding models across 8 tasks: (1) Bitext mining for translation matching, (2) Classification for training logistic regression classifiers, (3) Clustering for grouping sentences/paragraphs, (4) Pair classification for duplicate/paraphrase detection, (5) Reranking for relevance ranking, (6) Retrieval for finding relevant documents, (7) Semantic textual similarity (STS) for sentence similarity assessment, and (8) Summarization for scoring machine-generated summaries. The benchmark is intended for both research and industry applications to select appropriate embedding models for specific use cases.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is released as open-source software with versioning at both dataset and software levels to ensure reproducibility. The benchmark includes a public leaderboard on Hugging Face Hub. The maintainers welcome community contributions of tasks, datasets, or metrics via pull requests. JSON files corresponding to all results are made available with the benchmark. The project supports automatic submission format for leaderboard additions.

name.evidence: To solve this problem, we introduce the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB).

description.evidence: MTEB spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. Through the benchmarking of 33 models on MTEB, we establish the most comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings to date.
